content.title: Industries we build websites for
content.answerBlock: Calwebtech designs and builds websites, ecommerce platforms and web applications for manufacturers, distributors, retail and D2C brands, SaaS companies, healthcare providers, real estate firms, hospitality businesses, professional services firms and education providers. Each industry page covers the problems a website in that sector has to solve, the systems it connects to and, where we have published it, the work we delivered there.
content.intro: Tiered pricing, fitment data, compliance copy, multi-location booking. The parts that break generic builds are the parts we have shipped before.

approach.heading: Why does industry experience change how a website is built?
approach.intro: A website that fits one sector well usually fails another in the details. These are the details we settle before design starts.

items.title: The data model comes first
items.body: A distributor's catalogue, a clinic's locations and a hotel's room types are not pages. We model them as content types your team edits, so the site matches how the business actually works.

items.title: Integrations are scoped before design
items.body: ERP, practice management, MLS and property management systems decide what a website can promise. We check what their interfaces allow in discovery, not halfway through the build.

items.title: Compliance is designed in
items.body: Accessibility, consent, pricing disclosure and data handling rules shape forms and templates. Designing for them from the first wireframe costs far less than retrofitting them after launch.

items.title: Leads stay in a database you own
items.body: Every enquiry, booking and application lands in your own database with its source attached, so sector-specific routing and reporting are yours to change.
